message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

If you need up‑to‑date information, you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and you’ll see the current AQI, pollutant levels, and health recommendations. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and view the live AQI, forecast, and historical data. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or smartphone weather widgets) | Many include an AQI indicator for major cities. |
| **Local news sites** | They often report on smog alerts and air‑quality advisories. |

If you’re interested in a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They usually pull the latest data from one of these services.
